title: BNCI 2015-006 Music BCI dataset
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 11 healthy participants performing a multi-streamed musical oddball task designed to investigate auditory attention and brain-computer interface applications. Participants selectively attended to one of three concurrent instruments in polyphonic music clips while detecting deviant patterns, with EEG signals recorded at 64 channels and preprocessed to 250 Hz sampling rate. The study demonstrates that attended instrument selection can be classified from ongoing EEG with 91% mean accuracy using linear discriminant analysis, establishing proof-of-concept for music-based brain-computer interfaces.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired from 64 active electrodes (10-10 montage, Brain Products actiCAP) at 1000 Hz with left mastoid reference and forehead ground. Online bandpass filtering (0.016-250 Hz) was applied. Preprocessing included downsampling to 250 Hz, Chebyshev lowpass filtering (42 Hz passband, 49 Hz stopband), epoching (-200 to 1200 ms relative to stimulus), baseline correction, and artifact rejection using min-max criterion (100 μV threshold on Fp1/Fp2). Classification employed linear discriminant analysis with shrinkage covariance on spatio-temporal features extracted from three time intervals across 63 electrodes, evaluated using leave-one-clip-out cross-validation.
